conviction_note: A mild long lean. The sell-off from 445 to 336 is mostly a sector and election de-rating (ITA -18% Aug-Oct; -9.8% on 4 Nov). Street FY27 EPS $12.24 is only +4% on a FY26 base that holds about $0.70 of tariff refund. Counterparties since the July call are mixed: LMT booked the PAC-3 multiyear and MV75 funding was settled, but the 787 is stuck at 8/mo and the A350 is below rate 4. Woodward's FY27 guide was bought (+8.7% in two sessions). Findings sum to +2.3. The scaled number is (2*0.57-1)*7.5 = +1.05, because Q3's beat-and-raise was sold -7% on quality and the main risk is a headline FY27 guide that reads small against the refund-inflated FY26 base.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY27 adjusted EPS $12.24 (+3.97%) and revenue $4.73B (+7.27%), per https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mog.a/forecast/ (S&P Global consensus, page checked 2026-11-10, read 2026-11-19).
next_guide.company_current_guide: None for FY27. CEO on the 2026-07-31 call: 'we haven't given our guidance for next year, but we're pretty confident' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055). FY26 guide is $4.4B, 14.1% adjusted operating margin, $11.65 +/- 0.10 and 70% FCF conversion.
next_guide.basis: Moog issues its first guide with the Q4 release: FY26 opened at about $10.00 EPS on $4.2B, about +15% on FY25 adjusted $8.69 (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4525063-moog-projects-9-percent-sales-growth-and-10-eps-for-fy26-as-backlog-hits-3b-record), and the stock rose 8.16% that day. Several things point to an initiation at or above the street: twelve-month backlog +23% at June, management saying missile upside is not yet in backlog, and the LMT PAC-3 multiyear now booked. Against that, the FY26 base carries about $0.70 of non-recurring tariff refund, 787/A350 rates are stalled, and peer Woodward guided margin expansion to moderate on capacity spending.

findings.finding: Street FY27 adjusted EPS is $12.24, only +4% on FY26 consensus of $11.77 (stockanalysis), but FY26 adjusted includes about $0.70 from the $30M IEEPA tariff refund that management called largely non-recurring. Ex-refund, the street needs about +12% from a clean base of about $11.0. Moog's last first guide (FY26: $10.00 vs FY25 $8.69, +15%) cleared a similar bar, its twelve-month backlog was +23% at June (vs street FY27 revenue +7.3%), and the CEO said on 31 Jul he was 'pretty confident' on FY27. Net: an initiation at or above $12.24 is more likely than not. The risk is a headline that management frames off the refund-inflated $11.65+ base, which the Earnings Whispers preview names as the outcome that 'would confirm market doubts'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First guide on 2025-11-21 (FY26 at $10.00, read as above consensus): +8.16%. The raise on 2026-07-31, where the raise was mostly refund, was sold -7.01%. Raises on 2026-01-30 and 2026-04-24 were bought +6.02% and +2.26% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 24-25% below the lowest sell-side target and -13.7% since the Q3 print, while FY27 consensus still sits at $12.24 (targets last moved in October). If the market believed in a clean +12% FY27, the stock would not trade at the low end of its 52-week range on a de-rated multiple. The drawdown says the market doubts the street number. The open question is whether management's first number validates it, and that is unpriced by construction until the release.
findings.independence: Q3 call transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055, 2026-07-31) for 'pretty confident' and missile upside not in backlog. Q3 8-K exhibit for the $30M refund at 270 bp and the twelve-month backlog of $3.3B (+23%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000067887/000162828026051250/ex991-73126.htm). FY26 first-guide precedent: https://seekingalpha.com/news/4525063-moog-projects-9-percent-sales-growth-and-10-eps-for-fy26-as-backlog-hits-3b-record. The street figure has a single aggregator source, so the size is capped.

findings.finding: Lockheed Martin booked the PAC-3 MSE multiyear into backlog in Q3 (record $292.0B backlog including $52.5B for the PAC-3 MSE multiyear; reported 2026-10-22) and raised its 2026 guide on PAC-3/THAAD/GMLRS output. On 31 Jul Moog's CEO said 'there is significant more upside to come on the missiles that is not yet reflected in our business backlog', with PAC-3 production step-ups of about 3x. Moog's Q4 (Sep quarter) backlog and FY27 Space & Defense guide are the first place the sub-tier award can show.
findings.link: Moog supplies the custom actuators for Lockheed's PAC-3 MSE interceptor, described as one of the largest awards in Moog Defense's history (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250129830001/en). Moog guided FY26 missile revenue to about $275M, roughly 6% of $4.4B sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog has been a driver: the record $3B backlog in Nov 2025 accompanied +8.16%. The deceleration of twelve-month backlog growth to 23% from 33% at Q3 is cited as part of the -7.01% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Moog has not spoken since 31 Jul. The preview (2026-11-15) still describes Lockheed's framework agreements as 'not yet in backlog' for Moog. If the market expected a backlog step-up, the post-Q3 backlog-deceleration narrative would have faded and the stock would not have fallen 13.7% since.
findings.independence: Moog Q3 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055) is a different document from Lockheed's release. The timing of Moog's sub-award booking is an inference: Moog has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Two of Moog's largest commercial programs are stalled at the OEM. Boeing said on 2026-10-27 that the 787 is holding at 8/month (not the planned 10) on engine and delivery issues. Airbus's CEO said on 2026-10-28 that the A350 had run 'below rate four' for some months or quarters, with only 38 A350 deliveries in 9M26 and three in September. Both points came after Moog's 31 Jul call, where the CEO said 787/A350 production plans were 'pretty consistent' with customer needs. They lean the FY27 Commercial Aircraft OEM guide cautious. Commercial Aircraft was $253.6M of $1,116.5M in Q3 (23%), with OEM only part of it, and the rest of the company (defense, industrial at +17-18%) must carry growth.
findings.link: Moog makes flight-control actuation for the Boeing 787 and high-lift actuation for the A350. On the Q3 call the analyst question on A350/787 sell-in vs assembly rates shows these are the programs the line turns on (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055). Commercial Aircraft is 23% of Q3 sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY26 outlook was already trimmed for commercial aircraft inventory timing (preview). No clean reaction to that line alone is visible in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Both counterparty statements came after Moog's last call, and Moog's FY27 commercial guide has not been set against them. But they were public weeks ago and the whole aerospace group traded on them, so this is a proxy that is partly priced. If the market had fully priced it, sell-side FY27 revenue (+7.3%) would have come down; targets last moved on 2026-10-13, before both releases.
findings.independence: Boeing Q3 release: https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-10-27-Boeing-Reports-Third-Quarter-Results (different document, same direction). Moog has not confirmed any impact; this is a transmission inference.

findings.finding: MV75 (Bell/Textron) funding gap closed: Congress approved a $350M Army reprogramming for FY26 MV75 funding, and about $300M was obligated during Textron's Q3 to cover costs already incurred by Textron and its suppliers. Textron had been self-funding since July. On 31 Jul Moog said some program spend was capped by a do-not-exceed limit already in its guidance, and the Earnings Whispers preview flagged 'limited visibility into early calendar 2027'.
findings.link: Moog is a flight-control supplier on Bell's V-280/MV75 (Military Aircraft segment, $245.2M in Q3). On the Q3 call management discussed V-280 work, Textron's workflow disruption and the do-not-exceed cap (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2943055).
findings.why_not_priced: The 15 Nov preview still lists MV75 visibility as a risk, so the resolution has not reached the Moog narrative. It is a supplier-cost catch-up that firms FY27 Military Aircraft rather than a new award, so it is small. MarketBeat page fetched as a search snippet only (403 on fetch).
findings.independence: https://finsee.ai/earnings/txt/2026/q3/en/ (Bell worked at its own expense after running through FY26 funds in July). Same underlying Textron call.

findings.finding: Peer Woodward initiated FY27 on 2026-11-18 at adjusted EPS $10.20-10.70 (vs FY26 consensus about $9.34, so +9-14%), total sales +6-10% and Aerospace sales +8-13%, and said margin expansion would moderate on capacity investment. The market bought an aerospace-component FY27 first guide that cleared a doubting bar. MOG.A rose +2.6% over the same two sessions (327.91 -> 336.36), so part of the read-through is already in.
findings.link: Both are flight-control and actuation suppliers to the Boeing/Airbus OEM programs (WWD Q4 Commercial OEM +26%) and to defense, both have an industrial segment, and both report a September fiscal year with a first FY27 guide in November. No shared revenue figure is available.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline has no peer read-through history.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MOG.A already rose 2.6% beside WWD's 8.7%. What is not priced is the template, a first FY27 guide sized off a clean base that the market rewarded. WWD's 'margin expansion will moderate' caution transfers too, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: WWD prices: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WWD?range=1mo&interval=1d. WWD preview with the 'fading tailwinds' framing: https://finviz.com/news/420898/woodward-closes-a-record-year-as-fading-tailwinds-put-its-fiscal-2027-outlook-on-trial.

findings.finding: Expectations reset. MOG.A sits at 336, -24.5% from its 17 Aug close, -13.7% since the Q3 print and 24-25% below even the lowest sell-side target ($417). Most of the drop lines up with sector events rather than Moog news: the aerospace and defense de-rating (ITA -17.9% from 14 Aug to 19 Oct), the -7.0% on 22 Oct, the day Lockheed reported, and -9.9%/-5.3% on 4-5 Nov after the Democratic congressional sweep. Short interest is low and only modestly rising (3.4% of class, DTC 3.3). An adequate guide therefore meets a lowered bar rather than the 30%-run-up bar of July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 came after a 30% three-month run-up and was sold -7.01%. Nov 2025 came after a weaker tape and was bought +8.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is visible in the price, which is the point. What is not settled is whether it reflects Moog's FY27 or the sector. If the market thought Moog's FY27 was impaired, analysts would have cut estimates, but FY27 EPS is still $12.24 and targets were only trimmed. The gap between targets and spot is the expectations cushion.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 bar: consensus EPS is $2.70 and revenue $1.12B (Earnings Whispers); the FY26 consensus of $11.77 implies about $2.78. Moog's own guide implies about $2.66 and $1.13B, so the street is at or slightly above the guide. Moog beat every FY26 quarter (Q2 adjusted EPS $2.64 vs $2.38; Q3 $3.72 including the refund). The Q4 print most likely lands in line to slightly above, inside the range the company already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 beat (+40% EPS) sold -7.01%. Q2 beat (+11%) bought +2.26%. Q1 beat bought +6.02%. The quarter itself has not reliably paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It lands inside the company's guide, and the street sits at or above the guide-implied figure. The only way it moves the stock is through quality, for example whether any further IEEPA refunds or tax items flatter it.
findings.independence: Q2 beat figures: https://www.tikr.com/blog/moog-nyse-stock-gains-as-aerospace-contractor-beats-earnings-estimates. Guide arithmetic: Q3 8-K exhibit.

MOG.A fell -9.8% on 4 Nov. Space & Defense plus Military Aircraft were $581M of $1,116.5M Q3 sales (52%). Management may hedge the FY27 defense outlook or face call questions on it, though the effect on FY27 (Oct 2026 - Sep 2027) orders is small and indirect.

findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock already took the hit. What remains is whether Moog's guide or call comments add a company-level confirmation. Macro-to-company transmission is unconfirmed by Moog.
findings.independence: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/20/defense-stocks-are-tumbling-as-wall-street-bets-on-a-democratic-sweep/ (sector pricing a sweep before the vote).

findings.finding: Data-center cooling pumps went from about $25M (FY25) to close to $100M (FY26) at about 1,300 pumps/week on three lines. Demand is mainly one hyperscaler through two CDU makers, and a next-generation in-row product (PeCAS 5 standard) reaches production in FY27. That gives Industrial (Q3 +18%) an FY27 growth driver outside aerospace and defense, with customer concentration as the stated risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction; the guidance rise from $50M to $100M came through the FY26 raises, which were bought in Jan and Apr.
findings.why_not_priced: Stated on the July call, so the level is known. The FY27 number for this line has not been given, and Industrial is the segment least exposed to the defense de-rating. Small.
findings.independence: https://www.webull.com/news/15330621674038272 (Simply Wall St, 2026-08-02: pump revenue about $25M to about $100M, single-hyperscaler risk). Same underlying call.

outside_window.finding: Textron flagged a possible $110-150M unfavourable catch-up on an MV75 LRIP award in 2027. If supplier pricing pressure follows, it lands on Moog's Military Aircraft after the window.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the skew (-2.68, upside paid, though the chain is thin at 515 OI) and leans against the run-up: the -2.3% 20d and -24.5% from the August high are read as a sector de-rating that lowers the bar, not as Moog-specific information. lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar has one source): FY27 street $12.24 rests on one aggregator, so the next_guide finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its last beat -7%): Q4 consensus-bar finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1, and p_up taken from 58 to 57.

Lesson 5 (proxy / unconfirmed transmission): 787/A350 counterparty finding cut from -0.8 to -0.5, because Moog said on 31 Jul that plans were consistent; LMT PAC-3 backlog timing cut from +0.8 to +0.6 because it is an inference on when Moog books its sub-award.

Lesson 3 (own caveat must reach the number): Woodward read-through cut from +0.7 to +0.5 because MOG.A already rose 2.6% alongside it; expectations finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6 because the drawdown is sector-driven rather than a Moog-specific bar reset.

Lesson 2 (tariff refund names split on guidance direction): confirmed that the refund is filed only through the guidance question, not as a one_off finding. No size change beyond the merge already made.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked (3.4%, DTC 3.3, not crowded); the only negatives are small and need no squeeze haircut. Left standing.
